description: The status precedence table of DESIGN v2.6 §B, written out in full: every combination of the four status inputs (16 rows) and the status the pill and the light bar show for it. Precedence: listening > speaking > thinking > (noController | idle). Live activity always outranks the missing controller, because the controller is optional (voice capture can start from the mic button or the keyboard); noController is only the resting state when nothing is happening and no pad is connected. Status names: noController, idle, listening, thinking, speaking.
function: AppState.derivedStatus(controllerConnected:isPTTActive:isSpeaking:isWorking:) — input {controllerConnected, isPTTActive, isSpeaking, isWorking} in, status name out
verifiedBy: DESIGN.md v2.6 addendum §B (precedence) and characterization of the Swift implementation (spec #94, ticket #125); Tests/PowerUpTests/StatusDerivationTests.swift. Rust: rust/powerup-core/tests/status.rs derivation_cases runs status::derived_status. Pure function, no device or harness involved.

cases.name: resting with a pad connected
cases.reason: Nothing is happening and a pad is there: the green Ready state.

cases.name: resting with no pad
cases.reason: The only row where No Controller shows: nothing is happening and no pad is connected.

cases.name: thinking with a pad
cases.reason: A running turn turns the light amber.

cases.name: thinking with no pad
cases.reason: A prompt sent from the keyboard still shows that the agent is working; the v1 order would have hidden it behind No Controller.

cases.name: speaking with a pad
cases.reason: A reply being read aloud turns the light purple.

cases.name: speaking with no pad
cases.reason: Replies still speak without a pad, so the pill must say so rather than No Controller.

cases.name: speaking while working, with a pad
cases.reason: Speaking outranks thinking: a summary or reply read aloud while the next turn already runs shows purple, not amber.

cases.name: speaking while working, no pad
cases.reason: Speaking outranks thinking and the missing pad at the same time.

cases.name: listening with a pad
cases.reason: A held trigger records: the light goes red.

cases.name: listening with no pad
cases.reason: The keyboard or mic-button capture path: the v1 order froze the pill on No Controller while recording, the bug v2.6 fixed.

cases.name: listening while working, with a pad
cases.reason: Listening outranks thinking: dictating the next prompt during a turn shows red, so the person knows they are being recorded.

cases.name: listening while working, no pad
cases.reason: Listening outranks thinking and the missing pad at the same time.

cases.name: listening while speaking, with a pad
cases.reason: Listening outranks speaking: the microphone being live matters more than playback (a capture normally stops speech first, but the flags can overlap for a moment).

cases.name: listening while speaking, no pad
cases.reason: Listening outranks speaking and the missing pad at the same time.

cases.name: everything at once, with a pad
cases.reason: Listening is the top of the order; nothing outranks a live microphone.

cases.name: everything at once, no pad
cases.reason: Listening is the top of the order even with no pad connected.
